newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany approves Czech reconciliation text.
newsitem.headline: Germany approves Czech reconciliation text.

text.p: The German government said on Thursday it had approved the text of a declaration intended to close the book on 50 years of post-World War Two mistrust with the Czech Republic.
Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel is due to go to Prague on Friday to initial the text, the product of almost two years' negotiation, with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec.
Germany hopes the declaration will pave the way to the kind of straightforward relations it now has with other neighbouring states invaded and occupied by the Nazis before or during World War Two.

The declaration contains mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for excessive brutality during the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans from the Sudetenland region of what was then Czechoslovakia.

But, in a reflection of the gap that still remains in the two countries' official views of the war and its aftermath, it skirts sensitive questions of compensation for both Czech and ethnic German victims of the war.
The main political critic of the declaration in Germany, the Bavarian-based Christian Social Union (CSU) which acts as mentor to the Sudeten Germans, had already signalled grudging acceptance.

The Sudeten Germans themselves, survivors and relatives of the 2.5 million ethnic Germans who were collectively blamed for the Nazi occupation and summarily driven out, have objected to the text but now appear to have little chance of changing it.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl is due to sign the declaration with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus in January and the presidents of the two countries will then address each other's parliaments to seal the matter.
